newsitem.title: UK: Snapshot of British Labour's legislative programme.
newsitem.headline: Snapshot of British Labour's legislative programme.

text.p: Following is a snapshot of the legislative programme unveiled by Britain's new Labour government in the Queen's speech on Wednesday.
The speech signals the formal opening of the parliament elected on May 1. It includes 22 bills plus four that the government hopes to introduce if time allows.
List of Bills --
* EDUCATION - to reduce class sizes
* EDUCATION - to raise educational standards
* BANK OF ENGLAND - to give the Bank operational independence to set interest rates
* COMPETITION - to stamp out anti-competitive practices
* STATUTORY RIGHT TO INTEREST ON DEBTS -- to give firms a statutory right to claim interest on late payments
* NATIONAL MINIMUM WAGE - to introduce a minimum wage after consultation with industry and employee groups
* CRIME AND DISORDER - to mete out swifter justice to persistent young offenders
* FIREARMS (AMENDMENT) - to ban all handguns in response to the Dunblane massacre
* NATIONAL HEALTH SERVICE (PRIVATE FINANCE INITIATIVE) -- to clarify the rights of National Health Service Trusts to enter into partnerships with the private sector
* NATIONAL LOTTERY (AMENDMENT) - to replace Camelot Group Plc as the organiser of Britain's national lottery when its franchise expires
* LOCAL AUTHORITY (CAPITAL RECEIPTS) - to enable capital receipts from the sale of council houses to be invested in housebuilding and renovation
* DATA PROTECTION - to give effect to 1995 EU directive to strengthen controls
* EUROPEAN CONVENTION ON HUMAN RIGHTS -- to incorporate into British law the main provisions of the European Convention on Human Rights
* FINANCE - to implement measures announced in forthcoming budget
* REFERENDUMS (SCOTLAND AND WALES) - to allow the people of Scotland and Wales to vote on devolved assemblies
* SCOTLAND - subject to referendum, would provide for establishment of Scottish parliament
* WALES - subject to referendum, would set up Welsh assembly
* GREATER LONDON AUTHORITY (REFERENDUM) - to vote on establishing a new strategic authority for London and a directly elected mayor
* REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT AGENCIES - to establish regional agencies in England, outside London
* NORTHERN IRELAND (EMERGENCY PROVISIONS) - legislation to combat terrorism
* NORTHERN IRELAND (PARADES AND MARCHES) - legislation to reduce tension over parades
* EUROPEAN COMMUNITIES (AMENDMENT) - to enact any decisions made at June's EU Amsterdam summit
Four bills not identified in the Queen's speech but which the cabinet agreed should be introduced in the first session
* SOCIAL SECURITY - to simplify decisions and hearing appeals
* IMMIGRATION APPEALS (AMENDMENT) - to extend appeal rights and set up body to deal with them
* WIRELESS TELEGRAPHY (RADIO SPECTRUM) - to charge competitive prices for use of the airwaves
* COMPREHENSIVE TEST BAN TREATY RATIFICATION - ban has been signed by 144 companies and will be ratified in parliament.
